direction.premise: A working field commander's topographic atlas, where a decision is drawn into the landscape and executed against another army.
direction.composition: The map occupies the working surface; portrait devices turn the whole battlefield ninety degrees, while a desktop command ledger sits beside the map.
direction.shapeLanguage: Thin rectangular regiment footprints, individual ranks, forked heraldic pennants, dashed future routes and an unrounded ruled command ledger.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Procedural ink contour lines and wooded clusters on muted survey paper, with solid colored regiment marks rather than polished tiles.
direction.paletteLogic: Muted greens encode the landscape, blue and russet identify opposing armies, and ivory supports text; pressure and route lines use the side colors.
direction.typography: A restrained Georgia heading recalls a printed field atlas; compact system labels keep numerical orders and status legible.
direction.signature: A hand-drawn command route ends in a ghost footprint showing formation orientation; later route stages have their own dashed marks and numbers.
direction.distinction: Compared with Doctrina's political atlas and Chernye Znamena's hex campaign, this map resolves continuous oriented footprints, timed multi-step paths and animated rank movement.

architecture.primaryVerb: Select a field regiment, draw its projected movement path, queue subsequent orders, and confirm a fixed-duration WEGO turn.
architecture.physicalFeedback: A drawn route immediately renders its numbered stage and footprint; the committed round moves opposing regiments according to contact, acceleration and formation cohesion.
architecture.spatialRationale: A portrait player can see the two fronts along the long axis instead of a narrow horizontal strip; selection exposes the command ledger while landscape places it to the right.

comparisons.spatialDifference: A rotated battlefield and contextual command ledger replace the political atlas and strategic menu.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Players draw continuous regiment paths and review a simultaneous timed resolution rather than choose administrative actions.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The free-coordinate continuous field replaces a campaign layout divided into hexagons and economic panels.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Players chain physical maneuvers across time rather than issue a turn action to a grid cell.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The central surface is a zoomable topographic battlefield rather than a permanent file processing instrument.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Direct selection of a spatial regiment leads to a drawn path with a later simultaneous opposing response.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The map holds two colored armies and a contextual ledger rather than adjacent mathematical specimens.
comparisons.interactionDifference: An ordered unit trajectory is resolved by a timed tactical engine instead of editing discrete automaton rules.

production.renderer: Canvas directly represents continuous terrain, rank geometry and world-coordinate orders; DOM provides accessible command and report controls.
production.focalAsset: A procedural relief atlas and vector regiment markings are rendered by the app, with a distinct crossed-banner SVG install icon.

motion.character: Precise command strokes contrasted with physical acceleration, blocked formations and deliberate simulated turn playback.
motion.action: Drawing a regiment's movement route and confirming both armies' locked orders for a thirty-second resolution.
motion.anticipation: The chosen movement command activates route drawing and a dotted endpoint footprint previews the intended direction.
motion.response: The route follows the finger immediately and subsequent stages receive visible numbered dashed trajectories.
motion.followThrough: During replay the regiments move through time and retain new formation, casualties, morale and positions for the next turn.
motion.interruption: Pointer cancellation abandons the draft route; playback can pause, scrub or finish without altering the deterministic outcome.
motion.reducedMotion: Playback can be paused and scrubbed or skipped to the settled state; the route and battle ledger remain readable without animation.

evidence.expectedChange: The muster page is replaced by an interactive deployment map with separate blue and red armies, visible command tools and a deployment zone.

review.observations: Baseline Chromium and WebKit screenshots were reviewed. Portrait wasted vertical map space, and initial WebKit frames could show a blank atlas. The current implementation rotates the viewport and draws synchronously on resize. Current-build screenshot review is pending; status deliberately remains draft.
